requirements.requirement: Define the rowwise size-T block matrix-vector product with sequential reduction and zero padding.
requirements.evidence: padded returns zero beyond n. roundedProduct uses padded(A(i))(b*T+t)*padded(x)(b*T+t)*(1+E.mulError(i,b,t)). blockPartial sequentially sums T products, and computed sequentially sums B block partials for each row. sequentialSum starts with its first term and rounds all subsequent additions. blockCount=((n+T) dotminus 1) div T equals ceil(n/T) for T>0. Padded trailing additions still multiply prior accumulated contributions.

requirements.requirement: Prove the perturbation matrix identity and the entrywise gamma(T + ceil(n/T) - 1) bound.
requirements.evidence: Both targets explicitly assert the identity and |DeltaA(i,j)|<=gamma(k,u)*|A(i,j)| for every i,j. Here k=errorCount(n,T)=T+ceil(n/T)-1 and gamma(k,u)=k*u/(1-k*u). The constructed target proves these for DeltaA(i,j)=A(i,j)*(pathCoefficient(T,E,i,j)-1). pathCoefficient includes the product error and all inner and outer addition factors affecting the term: max(1,t)<=s<T and max(1,b)<=s<B, respectively.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the stated hypotheses and generality. Do not assume the conclusion or introduce a circular definition.
requirements.evidence: The hypotheses T>0 and u>=0 express positive block size and nonnegative unit roundoff implicit in the source. Valid imposes only absolute bounds on the relative errors of the elementary operations; these are the source standard rounding-model assumptions, not a desired algorithmic bound. Universal arbitrary valid traces cover executions under that model with no overflow or underflow. The remaining hypothesis is precisely (T+ceil(n/T)-1)*u<1. There are no divisibility, nonzero-entry, or positive-dimension restrictions. The computation and perturbation are independently defined.
